title: The Winter Ledger
premise: In the frozen port city of Vhalen, Mirabel Eriksen — a pearl diver's son indentured to the Ostmark Trading Company — has spent his life keeping his head down and his ledgers balanced. When a sealed letter arrives naming his family as conspirators in a smuggling plot that toppled a shipping magnate, Mirabel realizes the company intends to bury the truth along with his name. Armed only with his meticulous records, an unlikely alliance with the historian's daughter Sera, and fragments of his drowned father's memory, he races to get the real ledger on record before the victors' historians write him out of history. The book ends with Mirabel testifying before the harbor commission, trading his freedom for the truth, and finding that being remembered on his own terms is worth more than the life of quiet anonymity he once guarded.
about_author: M. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers from northern port towns before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: Salt in the Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet him at nineteen, copying invoices in the Ostmark counting house, hiding his diver's calluses under long sleeves. He keeps one private habit: recording small kindnesses in a hidden notebook. Emotional beat: quiet longing for a self beyond his indenture papers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Mirabel's POV, to his childhood aboard his father's diving boat — the last summer before the storm and the debt that indentured the family. His mother's silence about that night plants the first mystery. Emotional beat: grief braided with love.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A courier delivers a sealed letter addressed not to the company but to 'the Eriksen household.' His supervisor intercepts it; Mirabel glimpses the wax crest before it vanishes into the locked drawer. Emotional beat: dread arriving in ordinary packaging.

chapters.title: The Historian's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sera Lindqvist's POV. She works in her father's archive across the quay, cataloguing the magnate Halvard's estate after his suspicious death. She notices pages cut from the shipping manifests — and remembers Mirabel from a market argument over a mislabeled crate. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Summoned before the company factor, Brannoch, he is accused — gently, terrifyingly — of tampering. The intercepted letter named his family as Halvard's partners in a smuggled cargo. Brannoch offers protection in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: the trap closing softly.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mirabel breaks into the records room to copy the drawer's contents; Sera, pursuing the same missing pages, nearly catches him. Instead of betrayal they strike a wary bargain: her archive access for his inside knowledge. Emotional beat: two loners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Mother's Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He confronts his mother, who finally produces half of his father's old dive log — water-stained, coded. She begs him to stop digging: 'Some cargoes sink for a reason.' Emotional beat: love as a wall as much as a shelter.

chapters.title: The Drowned Cargo
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Decoding the dive log with Mirabel, they learn Halvard's final shipment was never grain — it was contraband arms, and the 'storm' that sank it was arranged. The company helped sink it, then helped bury the story. Emotional beat: revelation as vertigo.

chapters.title: Brannoch's Kindness
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Brannoch promotes him — visibly, publicly — a gilded muzzle. Colleagues who once ignored him now flatter or shun him. Mirabel understands he is being made complicit by comfort. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Icebound Harbor
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Winter seals the port; the commission that will write the official history convenes after thaw. Sera's father, pressured by company patrons, warns her off. She copies what she can anyway and hides it in plain sight among finished catalogs. Emotional beat: defiance in a quiet room.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A second sealed letter arrives — this time a threat, naming Sera. Someone inside their circle is reporting to Brannoch. Suspicion poisons the alliance just as they need it most. Emotional beat: trust cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: Old Wrecks, Older Friends
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He seeks out Tove, his father's former dive partner, now a drunk on the breakwater. Tove confirms he was paid to stay ashore the night of the sinking — and that Mirabel's father refused, which is why he went down. Emotional beat: inherited courage, inherited cost.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Keeps
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, intimate and reflective. He reads his hidden notebook of recorded kindnesses against his father's dive log and realizes both are the same act: testimony. He decides the ledger must go on public record, whatever it costs. Emotional beat: identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The informant strikes: the copied pages vanish from her father's archive, and her father is dismissed. Sera discovers the informant is her own cousin, a junior clerk buying his way out of debt. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Running the Ice
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With the original dive log and his own certified copies, Mirabel goes underground among the dockworkers' families who remember the Eriksen name kindly. Brannoch's men sweep the quarter. Emotional beat: the hunted discovering he belongs to something.

chapters.title: The Commission Convenes
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The harbor commission opens its inquiry into Halvard's death, and the company presents its sanitized history. Sera watches the victors' version take shape in real time — smooth, plausible, and false. Emotional beat: fury at how easily memory is rewritten.

chapters.title: A Name on the Record
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Against every warning, Mirabel walks into the commission hall and requests to testify. Brannoch, seated among the commissioners' patrons, smiles like a man watching a moth approach flame. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into stillness.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, the climax. He reads the dive log, the coded entries, and his own certified copies into the record, naming names — including Brannoch's role in arranging the sinking. Brannoch counters by exposing Mirabel's indenture, arguing a bonded man cannot swear an oath. Emotional beat: everything staked on truth's weight.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Bought
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Tove, sober for the first time in years, takes the stand to corroborate; then Sera's father, disgraced but unbowed, authenticates the archive gaps. The commission's patron bloc wavers as the room turns. Emotional beat: solitary acts becoming a chorus.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The commission rules the official history must be reopened; Brannoch resigns ahead of certain ruin. But Mirabel's testimony voids nothing of his indenture — he chooses to serve out his term rather than flee, so no one can call his word purchased. Emotional beat: victory with a price willingly paid.

chapters.title: The Open Ledger
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Spring returns. Sera publishes the corrected account with both their names on the title page, and her father's archive reopens with the restored pages. She and Mirabel stand where the market argument began, no longer strangers. Emotional beat: love that grew from shared truth.

chapters.title: What the Sea Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, coda. On the first dive-boat out after thaw, Mirabel scatters flowers where his father went down, carrying the completed ledger — his family's story, on the record, in his own hand. He writes one last entry in the notebook of kindnesses: his own name. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept.
